resources.title: Introducing System One Models & Jev
resources.description: Diogo Almeida introduces Jev, the System One framing, RLCD, launch demonstrations, and the qualifications behind the reported performance gains. The starting point for this collection.

resources.title: TypeSafe manifesto
resources.description: The company’s argument for models designed to make decisions inside software.

resources.title: The Bitterest Lesson
resources.description: Founder’s research perspective on the objectives and data used to train useful models. Background to the Jev launch.

resources.title: AI: too good to be true, too bad to be useful
resources.description: TypeSafe’s argument about the gap between conversational ability and dependable automation.

resources.title: Introduction and quick start
resources.description: The official entry point for sending state and typed questions to Jev.

resources.title: Choice, Score, and Noul
resources.description: Definitions of the three output primitives, including probability distributions and answer shapes.

resources.title: Confidence
resources.description: How TypeSafe distinguishes answer probability from confidence and uses them in workflows.

resources.title: Model reference
resources.description: Version identifiers, supported inputs, limits, and current service specifications.

resources.title: Jev 1.13 jaggedness
resources.description: First-party documentation of uneven capabilities and known weak spots. Essential context for evaluating launch claims.

resources.title: Patterns and cookbooks
resources.description: Implementation guides for routing, scoring, fan-out, classification, search, and other bounded decisions.

resources.title: Workflow evaluations
resources.description: Vendor-run workflow comparisons, examples, and methodology; reference-model agreement is not the same as human ground truth.

resources.title: Documentation index
resources.description: Machine-readable index of official documentation for deeper exploration.

resources.title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
resources.description: Launch discussion with founder participation, questions about the API, architecture disclosure, calibration, and evaluation.

resources.title: Jev in 25 Lines of Python
resources.description: A deliberately minimal, explicitly satirical local implementation using option-token probabilities; the discussion probes what this does and does not reproduce.

resources.title: Ollaya – Ollama for open-source, Jev-style decision models
resources.description: Discussion of a local runtime for open decision models and compatibility with the TypeSafe interface.

resources.title: Jeff – Jev-compatible 0.8B decision models, trained at home, ~30 ms
resources.description: Release discussion for Jeff’s small decision models, local inference, and training approach.

resources.title: Kev: Tiny Jev-like family of decision models built on top of Qwen3.5
resources.description: Kev release discussion covering open weights, implementation choices, comparisons, and model size.

resources.title: OpenAI is well positioned to fast-follow Jev
resources.description: Debate about incumbent model providers, product differentiation, and Jev-style interfaces; market predictions are opinions.

resources.title: Show HN: Jev Plays Pokémon Red
resources.description: A Pokémon Red demonstration and discussion of the role of game state, legal actions, and the surrounding agent harness.

resources.title: Jeeves. Reasoning improves Jev-like decision models
resources.description: Jeeves release discussion about adding reasoning to Jev-style classifiers.

resources.title: Jev-Leftpad
resources.description: A humorous left-padding package powered by model decisions; useful as community history, not an infrastructure recommendation.

resources.title: Language models for text classification: From bag-of-words to Jev
resources.description: Discussion of Sebastian Raschka’s history of text classification and explanation of Jev-style decision interfaces.

resources.title: I turned Jev into a (lousy) chatbot
resources.description: An experiment generating text through repeated character choices, illustrating the limits of using Jev as a chatbot.

resources.title: Reverse-engineered Jev-like model
resources.description: Early independently built Jev-like option scorer; “reverse-engineered” in the thread title does not establish access to TypeSafe’s architecture.

resources.title: Show HN: JevBench, a reproducible benchmark for typed decision models
resources.description: Discussion of JevBench, its evaluation design, and cross-model comparisons.

resources.title: Jev Can't Be Calibrated
resources.description: Debate about distribution-dependent calibration and what a probability returned by Jev means.

resources.title: Jev introduces a new shape of LLM—System One, aka Decision Models
resources.description: Simon Willison explains the interface, experiments, open recreations, and the difficulty of inspecting a numeric decision.

resources.title: Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev
resources.description: Sebastian Raschka places Jev in the history of classifiers, readout methods, and calibration; proposed internals are explicitly inferential.

resources.title: Building a Harness with Jev
resources.description: LangChain’s tutorial on integrating bounded decisions into an agent loop, including routing and evaluation.

resources.title: Building Prod with Jev and LangGraph
resources.description: LangChain’s worked document-review workflow combines Jev classifications, graph orchestration, and escalation.

resources.title: What is Jev? — Browserbase
resources.description: Browserbase explains how Stagehand can use Jev for bounded browser actions and fall back to an LLM.

resources.title: You could have built Jev
resources.description: Pete Sergeant explains option scoring and compares independent implementations; reproducing an interface does not prove model equivalence.

resources.title: Jev can’t be calibrated
resources.description: Alex Molas argues that calibration must be checked against the deployment distribution rather than assumed from a model-wide claim.

resources.title: Jev or a fine-tuned small model?
resources.description: Distil Labs reports a pipeline experiment comparing Jev and task-specific models on triage and invoice decisions. Results describe that vendor’s setup.

resources.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
resources.description: Cloudflare introduces Jev-compatible multimodal decision models and describes its RL fine-tuning platform. Includes architecture and deployment details; benchmark comparisons are vendor-reported.

resources.title: Jev for Python engineers
resources.description: Vercel demonstrates typed Choice, Score, and Noul calls through its experimental Python evaluation API, including classification and AST generation. The examples also discuss failure cases.

resources.title: Jev is Poorly Calibrated
resources.description: Dylan Black tests option probabilities against known physical distributions and probes arithmetic failures. An author-run distribution-matching study, rather than a universal calibration verdict.

resources.title: The $40M Moat Lasted Two Weeks
resources.description: Abuiliazeed discusses Clef and Strands Decider as evidence of growing competition around Jev-style decision interfaces. An opinion essay on model commoditization and agent architecture; its market conclusions and benchmark comparisons are the author’s interpretation.

resources.title: System One models like Jev can train their own replacements
resources.description: Sean Goedecke proposes collecting inputs and decisions from a working Jev application to train a task-specific classifier. A distillation design argument, resurfaced in discussion, rather than a measured deployment study.

resources.title: Laya author’s prior-work discussion
resources.description: First-person account linking earlier sales-prediction and confidence-routing work. Architectural equivalence and priority claims are disputed and are not established by this thread.

resources.title: Is Jev a new model class or a classifier?
resources.description: Community debate about novelty, zero-shot classification, and the difference between a useful product and a new architecture.

resources.title: Awesome Jev / TypeSafe — AbdelStark
resources.description: Broad community directory of integrations, demos, and independent tests. Used for discovery; listed projects should be checked at their original sources.

resources.title: Awesome Jev — heyjunpenn
resources.description: Larger community project catalog useful for discovering the long tail of Jev applications.

resources.title: Awesome Jev — Amal-David
resources.description: Community collection with projects, skills, demonstrations, and a curated social-post gallery.

resources.title: TypeSafe Python SDK
resources.description: Official synchronous and asynchronous Python client for Jev.

resources.title: TypeSafe JavaScript / TypeScript SDK
resources.description: Official client with inferred answer types and typed question helpers.

resources.title: TypeSafe Agent Skills
resources.description: Official integration guidance for coding agents and skill-compatible tools.

resources.title: System One Adapter
resources.description: Official adapter that runs the decision interface over other LLM APIs for comparisons; it does not expose Jev weights.

resources.title: WorkflowEvals
resources.description: Source code for TypeSafe’s workflow evaluations. Its reference answers come from other models.

resources.title: TypeSafe n8n nodes
resources.description: Official repository for connecting the TypeSafe API to n8n workflows.

resources.title: Vercel AI Gateway
resources.description: Provider announcement and usage examples for accessing Jev through AI Gateway.

resources.title: Cloudflare Workers AI
resources.description: Provider-maintained Jev model page and structured evaluation examples.

resources.title: OpenRouter Jev playground
resources.description: Provider playground for turning a task into typed Jev questions.

resources.title: Netlify AI Gateway
resources.description: Provider documentation covering gateway configuration and TypeSafe integration.

resources.title: Vercel AI SDK for Python: experimental Jev evaluation
resources.description: Apache-2.0 Python SDK with an experimental typed evaluation API for Jev through AI Gateway. Supports Choice, Score, and Noul questions; the date refers to the integration article, not repository creation.

resources.title: Jev Ultrafast
resources.description: Browser Use’s agent represents available browser actions as candidates and uses Jev to select operations and targets.

resources.title: Jev Browser
resources.description: Playwright navigation exposed as a library, CLI, and MCP server, with bounded action selection.

resources.title: Jev MCP — Python
resources.description: MCP server exposing classification, scoring, checking, matching, and screening through Jev.

resources.title: Jev MCP — Node
resources.description: MCP tools for evidence checks, ranking, candidate selection, extraction, and patch review.

resources.title: Jev-Mem
resources.description: Agent memory architecture using fast decisions for organization and retrieval, with a separate model for answer synthesis.

resources.title: Jev Form Fill
resources.description: MIT-licensed Chrome extension that uses Jev to propose exact source-text values for form fields. Users review proposals before applying them; readback and undo are provided, while form submission remains manual. Requires hosted API access.

resources.title: jev-map
resources.description: MIT-licensed Python CLI and MCP server mapping functions to tests through static analysis and optional Jev-scored links. Records the evidence behind each link; missing links do not establish that a test can safely be skipped.

resources.title: DuckDB Jev
resources.description: DuckDB extension for Jev-backed predicates, classification, and scores over rows.

resources.title: pg-jev
resources.description: PostgreSQL extension for Jev-based row filtering, classification, and scoring. Version 0.2.1 adds local Jev-compatible servers without API keys and clarifies cache memory bounds. Public code uses the PostgreSQL license; hosted inference remains a separate service.

resources.title: jev — CLI and skill
resources.description: Community command-line wrapper supporting direct TypeSafe and OpenRouter backends.

resources.title: Jev Java
resources.description: Community Java client with typed questions and configurable retries.

resources.title: jev — Haskell
resources.description: Community Haskell client with composable typed questions and probability-preserving responses.

resources.title: Jev Doc Search
resources.description: VectifyAI uses Jev choices to navigate PageIndex document trees and select relevant PDF pages without an embedding index. Public Apache-2.0 code; hosted model access is a separate dependency.

resources.title: Laya
resources.description: Independent encoder-based decision models with English, multilingual, and workflow-specialist checkpoints; includes training and local serving.

resources.title: Kev
resources.description: Qwen-based family with released decision checkpoints, training code, evaluation suites, and TypeSafe-compatible serving.

resources.title: Bespoke Nimble
resources.description: Independent decision model with a contrastive data-curation recipe and public benchmark comparisons. Its authors state it was not distilled from Jev.

resources.title: Jeff — firelex
resources.description: Small decision models with local inference and domain adapters; distinct from other projects also called Jeff.

resources.title: Jeeves
resources.description: PostHog’s reasoning decision model, adding a diffusion drafter to a Qwen-based classifier; not a strictly one-pass decision model.

resources.title: Contrastive Language Models
resources.description: Contrastive state/action modeling with a TypeSafe-compatible API and an independently released 8B model.

resources.title: Vev
resources.description: Independent visual and textual decision models based on Qwen3.5, with 4B and 9B releases.

resources.title: WebJev
resources.description: Decision-model fine-tune specialized for browser actions; includes live-web data and evaluation harnesses.

resources.title: NanoJev
resources.description: Compact 0.6B model and training pipeline for parallel decisions in game environments; its scope is narrower than general hosted Jev.

resources.title: this-that-model-1.0
resources.description: A 2B typed-decision model with a research preprint. Reported speed and cost depend on its hardware and evaluation setup.

resources.title: Clef and Clef-flash
resources.description: Cloudflare releases independent multimodal decision models with Jev-compatible interfaces, using Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones respectively. Weights and decision-head inference code are available under Apache-2.0.

resources.title: Strands Decider 2B
resources.description: Independent Qwen3.5-2B-Base decision model with LoRA and a pointer readout for runtime-supplied Choice, Score, and Noul questions. Code and weights are Apache-2.0; training data retain their source licenses.

resources.title: GEV-26B-Decide
resources.description: AutoTrust decision model based on Gemma 4 26B-A4B, formerly named JEV-Gemma4-26B-A4B with unchanged weights. Adapter, head, and calibration files use Apache-2.0; the backbone retains Gemma terms. Original release date is unverified.

resources.title: Gutsy
resources.description: Small Qwen3.5-0.8B decision model exposing a Jev-style API through llama.cpp, with CPU-oriented GGUF quantizations. The repository and released model weights use Apache-2.0; upstream training datasets have separate terms.

resources.title: Tasksource-JEV-Nano v0
resources.description: Apache-2.0 weights for a compact ModernBERT/LateOn-based decision model using token-level late interaction to score runtime options. The card includes PyLate inference examples and author-reported evaluations. No exact original release date was verified.

resources.title: Jevling-E2B-v1
resources.description: Gemma 4 E2B-based typed decision fine-tune emphasizing Traditional Chinese kiosk transcripts, with Safetensors and GGUF weights. The checkpoint and base model declare Apache-2.0; its custom runtime is a separate artifact. Original release date is unverified.

resources.title: Chinese-Jev
resources.description: Chinese decision-model training, calibration, and evaluation code. The project lists trained Chinese-Jev weights as planned, so this entry is not a downloadable-weight release.

resources.title: Ollaya
resources.description: Local runtime for pulling and serving multiple decision-model families behind a TypeSafe-compatible API. Independent of Ollama and TypeSafe.

resources.title: AnyJev
resources.description: Nokia Applied Research’s library for typed readouts from open LLMs, including option-bias correction and calibration modes.

resources.title: SemIf-OpenJev
resources.description: Open-model option scoring and semantic conditionals; formerly named OpenJev and SemIf. This is an independent implementation.

resources.title: OpenJev SGLang
resources.description: Prefill-only decision serving over open models using SGLang.

resources.title: OpenJev — DiffusionGemma
resources.description: Independent TypeSafe-compatible server reading typed decisions from DiffusionGemma, with NVIDIA and Apple silicon paths.

resources.title: open-jev — daseinlabs
resources.description: Local Gemma option scorer using shared context and candidate sequence likelihoods.

resources.title: Jevlike
resources.description: Independent model and training starter that scores a changing set of candidate options in one pass.

resources.title: LibLayaX
resources.description: MIT-licensed shared library and C API built on laya.cpp for embedding Laya decisions inside an application without a separate server. Targets desktop and server platforms; model weights are downloaded separately from the Laya publisher.

resources.title: JevBench
resources.description: Independent multi-model benchmark with versioned scoring and results. Composite rankings depend on the published accuracy, calibration, latency, and cost methodology.

resources.title: Jevals
resources.description: Public benchmark suites and per-decision results for hosted Jev and comparator models.

resources.title: Jev Decision Index
resources.description: Interactive community comparison of decision-model systems hosted as a Hugging Face Space.

resources.title: Janus
resources.description: Calibration and cascade experiments using Jev and a larger fallback model on labeled classification tasks.

resources.title: jev-certify
resources.description: Conformal routing and auditing toolkit with a CLINC150 study; its guarantees depend on calibration and deployment assumptions.

resources.title: Jev benchmarking — AppliedMachineLearning-Lab
resources.description: Code accompanying the 37-dataset Jev evaluation; keep model versions and request templates fixed when reproducing it.

resources.title: RLCDAlignBench
resources.description: Benchmark of typed decisions for detecting alignment failures, with code and data linked from its paper.

resources.title: JevOut
resources.description: Research code for testing whether natural-looking context changes can redirect a decision model.

resources.title: DoubtBench
resources.description: Evaluates Jev and other decision models against human disagreement using typed questions derived from HelpSteer2. Reports accuracy, calibration, and distribution agreement. Code is MIT; derived data are CC BY 4.0. Results are maintainer-run.

resources.title: Tasksource typed decisions
resources.description: Recasts public task datasets into Choice, Score, and Noul supervision, including soft targets and grouped questions. Offers a smaller default mix and a full training set. Licenses remain source-dependent, with per-row provenance and usage labels.

resources.title: Korean JEV Benchmark
resources.description: Publishes 25,418 Korean finite-choice items and an October 4 comparison of hosted Jev with local model configurations. Serving precision, prompts, and probability readouts differ. Data licenses remain source-dependent; this is a curated derivative, not a new human-annotation study.

resources.title: Jev Cookbook
resources.description: Runnable recipes for support triage, classification, search, data cleanup, and browser actions.

resources.title: Jev Explained
resources.description: Interactive educational playground for observing typed decisions and probabilities.

resources.title: Jev Showcase
resources.description: Unofficial operator lab, smart-home examples, and a TypeScript harness.

resources.title: JEV-Star
resources.description: Research implementation combining Jev action selection with longer-horizon StarCraft II planning.

resources.title: Jev chat
resources.description: Character-by-character generation experiment built on a decision interface; deliberately illustrates an awkward use case.

resources.title: Jev Leftpad
resources.description: Satirical package that uses model decisions for string padding.

resources.title: Jevspresso and @xstate/jev
resources.description: Simulated espresso bar combining XState with Jev: the state machine enumerates currently valid actions and Jev selects among them. Includes a reusable integration package and evaluation scenarios. Public source is available, but no repository license was identified.

resources.title: Jevboard
resources.description: MIT-licensed Windows proof of concept that asks Jev to reconsider Bopomofo homophone choices from Microsoft IME candidates. Suggestions require user acceptance; the external candidate-scanning workflow is experimental and can be slow.

resources.title: Evaluating and Benchmarking the System One Model Jev
resources.description: Evaluates Jev on 37 datasets with frozen prompts and full evaluation splits. Covers calibration, multilingual behavior, and sensitivity to answer formats.

resources.title: Evaluating Decision Models for Text Annotation in Computational Social Science
resources.description: Studies computational social-science annotation, comparing accuracy, confidence, and the economics of escalation to LLMs.

resources.title: Jev in the Wild: A Data-Driven Analysis of the Jev Model's Functionality, Applications and Ecosystem
resources.description: Analyzes 2,170 public Jev-related GitHub projects, distinguishing ecosystem activity from concentrated public attention.

resources.title: Typed Decision Models: An Early Evidence Audit and Evaluation Checklist
resources.description: Reviews 28 early papers and derives an evaluation checklist. An early evidence map, not a settled verdict on the model class.

resources.title: Judgement in the Age of Jev: From Evaluation Scarcity to Evaluation Abundance
resources.description: A conceptual organizational perspective on inexpensive machine evaluation, motivated by Jev. Develops a conditional Jevons-style hypothesis and examines authority, reliance, and complementary costs; not an empirical validation of the product.

resources.title: Fast Models, Slow Evidence: A Paired and Self-Audited Evaluation of System-1 Decision Models for LLM Agent Harnesses
resources.description: Compares Laya and hosted Jev on 11 agent decision points with paired inputs and robustness variants. Audits its own pipeline, documenting how omitted costs, in-sample thresholds, and gate-level metrics distorted deployment conclusions.

resources.title: Benchmarking System One decision models against trained classifiers and language models for automated decision gates
resources.description: Compares typed decision models, trained classifiers, and generative models on matched decision-gate tasks. Examines supervision, calibration, out-of-scope acceptance, label swaps, and cascade costs; rankings depend on the task and operating conditions.

resources.title: Beyond Calibration: Do a Typed-Decision Model's Probabilities Obey the Probability Axioms?
resources.description: Checks logical consistency across related probability questions, distinguishing probability coherence from accuracy and calibration.

resources.title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure
resources.description: Tests Jev as a first-stage evaluator and routes uncertain decisions to a stronger judge. Benefits vary with workload and reasoning demands.

resources.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It
resources.description: Changes option names while preserving their rubrics to expose semantic label bias despite valid output types.

resources.title: Just Ask Jev: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions as a Zero-Shot Detector of AI Alignment Failures
resources.description: Introduces RLCDAlignBench to study zero-shot detection of alignment failures, including the influence of wording and supplied context.

resources.title: JEV vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places
resources.description: Compares rubric judges and shows why correlated errors can limit the accuracy gains of a confidence-based cascade.

resources.title: Beyond Answer Confidence: A Controlled Audit of Self-Knowledge in a Black-Box Decision Model
resources.description: Audits whether Jev confidence tracks missing knowledge using controlled information changes and surface-cue interventions. Distinguishes answer calibration from reliable knowledge-boundary detection and tests targeted sufficiency questions.

resources.title: When the Right Answer Is Missing: An Arithmetic-Dependent Rejection Bottleneck in Jev
resources.description: Tests arithmetic decisions when no offered answer is valid. Finds a rejection bottleneck relative to answer-present tasks and evaluates binary verification and development-set thresholds as mitigations.

resources.title: Labels Override Definitions in Jev-Style Typed Decision Models
resources.description: Tests whether open typed-decision models follow option definitions or short labels. Prompt-rendering interventions isolate label bias in several implementations; results concern the tested open models and should not be assumed to describe hosted Jev.

resources.title: More Choices, Fewer Decisions: Ordinal-Scale Bias in JEV-like Direct-Decision Models
resources.description: Studies compression of ordinal decision scales in Jev and open Kev models. Separates scale use from accuracy, label imbalance, and option order, then tests targeted post-training on open models as a mitigation.

resources.title: Decision Hijacking: Prompt Injection Attacks on Jev's Typed Probabilistic Decisions
resources.description: Measures prompt-injection effects on allowed action probabilities and selections; schema constraints do not eliminate decision manipulation.

resources.title: Calibrated Decision Models for Autonomous Penetration-Testing Harnesses: JEV and Laya as System One Decision Layers for LLM-Driven Pentest Agents
resources.description: Explores Jev and Laya as decision layers in penetration-testing agents. The reported two-run case study is exploratory, not strong causal evidence.

resources.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models
resources.description: Optimizes ordinary-looking context additions that flip initially correct decisions toward a fixed wrong option.

resources.title: SecJev: Bringing Security Expertise to System One Decision Models
resources.description: Introduces security-specialized Kev-based decision models spanning 0.8B–9B parameters and a corpus covering 14 tasks. Studies domain adaptation, transfer, and capture-dependent false alarms. The authors report releasing artifacts; public artifact locations were not independently confirmed.

resources.title: JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces
resources.description: Builds and revises compositional action spaces to connect natural-language tasks with finite probabilistic exploration.

resources.title: Jev-Mem: System-One-Controlled Agentic Memory for Efficient AI Agents
resources.description: Separates memory-management decisions from answer generation using a System One controller and a multi-relational memory graph.

resources.title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
resources.description: Studies a Jev-first agent controller with stronger-model fallback and examines when it improves on inexpensive generative cascades.

resources.title: JEV-Star: Fast, Low-Cost StarCraft II Control with Language-Model Planning
resources.description: Combines fast Jev actions with persistent LLM planning for StarCraft II; the comparison does not isolate planning from all harness changes.

resources.title: Harness Tokenomics: A Router for the Enterprise Agentic Control Plane
resources.description: Examines model routing while accounting for prompt-cache ownership and session boundaries. Savings are based on the paper’s workload and pricing assumptions.

resources.title: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents
resources.description: Uses occasional VLM planning with Jev choosing actions from an Android accessibility-tree action space.

resources.title: Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation
resources.description: Separates evaluation of supplied outcomes from predicting those outcomes across games, ALFWorld, and robot control. Tests whether host-code lookahead and simulation improve Jev action selection.

resources.title: Student-Guided Teacher Distillation for Efficient LLM Task Routing: Positioning Against Jev-Style System-1 Classifiers
resources.description: Studies ModernBERT student and DeBERTa teacher distillation for a fixed 60-category task router. Positions the method against Jev-style classifiers; reported evaluation is preliminary, with broader held-out and human-reviewed checks still in progress.

resources.title: this-that-model-1.0: A typed decision model that decides in 30 ms, for a millionth of a cent
resources.description: Presents a 2B model with a direct typed readout. Includes released weights and discusses weaknesses on multi-step arithmetic.

resources.title: Universal Fractal Natural Language Decision Map: Real-Time Edge Triage Across Heterogeneous Domains
resources.description: Proposes a fractal computation approach to typed edge decisions and reports JevBench results. Its unusual claims remain author-reported and require independent validation.

resources.title: Visual Jev: Accurate and Efficient Decisions from Shared Visual Context
resources.description: Shares visual context across independent questions and separates quality gains from post-training from speed gains due to shared execution.

resources.title: NumericJev: Jev-like LLM Numerical Decoding with Multiway Decision Trees
resources.description: Uses multiway decision trees to obtain numerical outputs at a chosen resolution from structured-choice models without additional training.

resources.title: From Text Decisions to Pixels: An Study of Jev-Style Visual Choice Model
resources.description: Introduces PixelJev for decisions over images and supplied candidates, studying adaptation, calibration, and transfer across visual tasks.

resources.title: LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them
resources.description: Extracts Jev-style option probabilities from ordinary LLMs using bracketed numeric identifiers. Compares training-free readouts with fine-tuning; gains depend on backbone and task, with KL anchors intended to preserve generation behavior.

resources.title: OpenJev-RLCD: A Working RLCD Implementation
resources.description: Presents an independent two-stage RLCD implementation that calibrates probabilities over sampled rationales before reinforcement learning. Compares with SFT and RLVR on reasoning tasks; not a reproduction of proprietary Jev training.

resources.title: JET: Justification Evaluation in Transformer
resources.description: Uses pretrained language and vision-language models for finite-choice decisions without additional training. Studies shared-prefix computation, cache management, and optional reasoning on consumer hardware, with hosted Jev as an external reference.

resources.title: Type-Safe Decision Frameworks for Agentic 5G Control: A Theory-Driven Testbed Characterization of Where They Can Be Applied
resources.description: Compares hosted Jev, a typed encoder, and an LLM retrofit on a 5G control testbed, examining deadlines, question sensitivity, and escalation.

resources.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
resources.description: Evaluates bounded intent interpretation with shared admission and scheduling logic, measuring decision overhead and timely service completion.

resources.title: Fast Intent-Driven Service Orchestration with Jev for 6G Edge Networks
resources.description: Studies Jev-based intent activation for 6G edge services using network simulation, shared queues, and a real image-reading service.

resources.title: Jev-IDS: System One Models for Network Intrusion Detection
resources.description: Evaluates typed Jev decisions for intrusion detection under scarce labels on a 300-flow NSL-KDD pilot. Reports accuracy, false-alarm, latency, and cost tradeoffs; the small pilot limits generalization.

resources.title: A First Glance at Jev for Network Traffic Classification: Accuracy, Processing Time, and Cost
resources.description: Examines Jev traffic classification from early packet features on CESNET-QUICEXT-25. Compares accuracy, processing time, and cost with LLMs and trained tree ensembles, noting differences in supervision and service configuration.

resources.title: Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks
resources.description: Introduces Chinese-language decision training and CJ-Bench, including domain specialists and on-device experiments. Weights were still pending in the checked repository.

resources.title: Open-Jev Judgments on CallScreenBench: Calibrated One-Pass Scam Screening with a Small Language Model
resources.description: Studies JevLite for per-turn scam-call screening. Synthetic calls and test-set exposure limit the scope of the reported results.

resources.title: Calibrated Decisions at Scale: Converting Police Crash Narratives into Probabilistic Crash Variables with a System One Model (Jev)
resources.description: Converts crash narratives into probabilistic variables with a typed schema and audits decisions against human judgments and coded records.

resources.title: JEVQA - Video Quality from Metadata, Bitstream, and Pixel Features with a General-Purpose Decision Model
resources.description: Predicts video quality from supplied metadata and derived features; this is not native video understanding by hosted Jev.

resources.title: Jev for Scientific Decisions: Evaluating Semantic Choices and Their Consequences
resources.description: Tests semantic choices that feed scientific calculations and distinguishes correct final labels from correct intermediate relations.

resources.title: KITE: Scaling Jev Population Experiments with Sparse Flagship Calibration
resources.description: Caches decision kernels over unique states for population simulations and uses sparse stronger-model anchors with explicit uncertainty accounting.

resources.title: Can Jev Judge Radiology Reports? Evaluating a System One Model for Clinical Factuality
resources.description: Tests Jev as a reference-based judge of radiology-report factuality. Report agreement and clinical error detection are evaluated separately.

resources.title: Same Scores, Different Decisions: Evaluating JEV and Language Models for Legal Document Understanding
resources.description: Evaluates contract inference under repeated and changed request conditions, showing why aggregate accuracy can hide unstable individual decisions.

resources.title: HydroJEV: A one-second, training-free screen for cyber-attack and fault attribution in water distribution networks
resources.description: Studies Jev for cyberattack and fault triage in simulated water networks. A rule-confirmed gate routes uncertain cases to a stronger reviewer; the sealed simulation experiments do not establish operational safety.

resources.title: Decision-Oriented Recommendation Reranking: An Empirical Study of Jev
resources.description: Studies Jev recommendation reranking across Amazon Reviews domains and candidate sets. Compares ranking quality and latency with conventional and language-model baselines; hosted-service conditions affect the practical tradeoffs.

resources.title: OmniMed-Jev: Calibrating LVLM Confidence for Trustworthy Medical Multimodal Decisions via System One
resources.description: Investigates typed confidence calibration for medical multimodal decisions using a shared vision-language backbone. Interface and training differences complicate attribution; the experiments do not establish clinical readiness.

resources.title: Jev in Medicine: A Benchmark Evaluation
resources.description: Evaluates Jev on medical questions and diagnostic cases, comparing accuracy, calibration, abstention, latency, and cost with GPT-6 Sol. Results differ sharply by task; this benchmark does not establish clinical readiness.
